guardrails: Every analytical review must resolve to an existing canonical occurrence_id.
Analytical evidence is governed separately from canonical provenance; citing it does not reassign source_id or alter canonical truth.
Expected values and actual values must remain distinct objects even when numerically equal.
A surprise label must identify its comparison basis; no surprise may be inferred solely from observed market movement.
Every market-movement assertion requires an evidence reference, measurement window and measurement precision.
Market movement does not establish causality. interaction_type, causal_status and confidence must be explicit.
Any connection stronger than NOT_A_CAUSAL_CLAIM requires at least one alternative explanation; stronger causal support requires independent evidence beyond temporal sequence.
Second-order effects must distinguish observed outcomes from prospective watch items.
Intrinsic importance and expected market sensitivity are canonical metadata and must not be overwritten by observed response.
The analytical layer must be able to conclude NO_CLEAR_SURPRISE, NOT_ESTABLISHED or NOT_A_CAUSAL_CLAIM without penalty.
